subtopicTitle: Moment of inertia of: rod (about end, centre), disk, ring, sphere (solid, hollow), cylinder

cards.front: What is the moment of inertia of a thin rod of mass $M$ and length $L$ about an axis perpendicular to the rod and passing through its center?
What is the moment of inertia of a thin rod of mass $M$ and length $L$ about an axis perpendicular to the rod and passing through one of its ends?
Derive the moment of inertia of a thin rod of mass $M$ and length $L$ about an axis perpendicular to the rod and passing through its center.
cards.back:
Consider a differential mass element $dm$ at a distance $x$ from the center. The linear mass density is $\lambda = M/L$. So, $dm = \lambda dx = (M/L)dx$. The moment of inertia $I = \int r^2 dm$. For this rod, $r=x$. The integration limits are from $-L/2$ to $L/2$. 
$$I = \int_{-L/2}^{L/2} x^2 \left(\frac{M}{L}\right) dx$$
$$I = \frac{M}{L} \int_{-L/2}^{L/2} x^2 dx$$
$$I = \frac{M}{L} \left[ \frac{x^3}{3} \right]_{-L/2}^{L/2}$$
$$I = \frac{M}{L} \left[ \frac{(L/2)^3}{3} - \frac{(-L/2)^3}{3} \right]$$
$$I = \frac{M}{L} \left[ \frac{L^3}{24} - \left(-\frac{L^3}{24}\right) \right]$$
$$I = \frac{M}{L} \left[ \frac{2L^3}{24} \right]$$
$$I = \frac{M}{L} \left[ \frac{L^3}{12} \right]$$
$$I = \frac{1}{12}ML^2$$

cards.front: State the moment of inertia of a uniform disk of mass $M$ and radius $R$ about an axis passing through its center and perpendicular to its plane.
State the moment of inertia of a thin uniform ring of mass $M$ and radius $R$ about an axis passing through its center and perpendicular to its plane.
What is the moment of inertia of a solid sphere of mass $M$ and radius $R$ about an axis passing through its center (i.e., its diameter)?
What is the moment of inertia of a thin-walled hollow sphere of mass $M$ and radius $R$ about an axis passing through its center (i.e., its diameter)?
Explain intuitively why a hollow sphere has a greater moment of inertia than a solid sphere of the same mass and radius about an axis through their centers.
cards.back: The moment of inertia depends on how mass is distributed relative to the axis of rotation ($I = \sum m_i r_i^2$). For a hollow sphere, all its mass is concentrated at the maximum possible radius $R$ from the center. For a solid sphere, much of its mass is closer to the center ($r < R$). Since mass further from the axis contributes more to $I$, the hollow sphere has a larger moment of inertia ($2/3 MR^2 > 2/5 MR^2$).

cards.front: What is the moment of inertia of a solid cylinder of mass $M$ and radius $R$ about its central longitudinal axis?
cards.back: $I = \frac{1}{2}MR^2$ (This is the same as a disk, as a cylinder can be thought of as stacked disks).
